blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings rose from 161 in June to 165 in September (+2.5%), and it took 49.8% of the city’s 215 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 71 in June to 69 in September (−2.8%), and it took 13.8% of the city’s 318 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out Abbotsford East for detached houses in June, July, August (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in September (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in July, August (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June, September (a buyers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Lots and land in Abbotsford East

items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default — and effectively the only verified — land form: the research records the detached stock as freehold, under City residential zones RS3, RS5 and RS6, "from established streets along Old Yale Road to newer subdivisions on the McKee and Eagle Mountain slopes." A bare lot sold in one of those subdivisions is a fee-simple parcel: no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fees — zoning, the OCP and any registered covenants or building scheme on title govern instead. An exact strata/freehold split for the sub-area is UNVERIFIED.

Lot character, AS THE RESEARCH STATES IT: RS3 minimum interior lot 540 m²; RS5 minimum interior lot 420 m²; RS6 is the Compact Lot Residential Zone used in newer subdivisions, with smaller compact lots (the research gives no RS6 minimum figure — UNCONFIRMED beyond "compact"). These are zoning-bylaw subdivision minimums as applied in City council reports, not a promise that any specific lot can be split — a lot already at or near its zone minimum has no subdivision room.

The McKee plan area is planned ground, not lot inventory: the McKee Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 3400-2023) plans the mountainside, with ground-oriented designations (Urban 2 – Ground Oriented in the plan material) and an open-space network of streamside setbacks, critical habitat, geotechnical areas and slopes over 40%. No developer or City source checked names a bare-land lot release, lot count or lot price in the McKee area — any "McKee lots" marketing figure is UNCONFIRMED.
Bare-land strata — its own form, stated plainly: a bare-land strata lot IS strata tenure on the lot itself — Form B, strata fees and registered bylaws apply to the lot; it is NOT fee-simple. (

Sage — 34365 Gladys Avenue (Diverse Properties) is a housing development, NOT a lot offering: confirmed on a developer source in the research as 176 apartment homes in five buildings with completion expected in 2026.

QUEUED — Marble Hill Place (2803 Marble Hill Drive, McMillan), counted nowhere: It is a built townhouse complex in any case, not land, and it stays QUEUED in every program for this ground, counted 0 here.
Cross-reference ONLY — The Argyle / King Road cluster: Built form, not land, named here only because east-side searches surface it.

ALR vs non-ALR split: the built east-side neighbourhoods are urban; the OCP carries an Agricultural Land Reserve map (Map 16), but ALR status inside the built neighbourhoods is not confirmed parcel by parcel in the research — UNCONFIRMED for any single lot until the ALC map and the parcel's title are checked.

Serviced vs unserviced: the urban east side is built subdivision ground; the research confirms no septic or well position inside the urban part (that item is listed unverified in the guide research), so servicing for any single lot — municipal water/sewer connection status, or well/septic on an acreage parcel toward Whatcom / Sumas Mountain — is UNCONFIRMED until the City's records for that parcel are read.

Assemblies / development sites / rezoning proposals: The McKee plan area is the area's designated future-growth ground (above); it is plan designation, not a for-sale assembly, and is never presented here as inventory.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Abbotsford East

items.t: "Abbotsford East" is the FVREB board sub-area name — one of nine sub-areas of the board community "Abbotsford" in the SnapStats data — not a single City of Abbotsford neighbourhood name. The City plans the east side through named neighbourhoods and plan areas including McMillan, Old Clayburn, East Townline, Whatcom and McKee, and the mountainside part is planned separately through the McKee Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 3400-2023), Schedule E of the Official Community Plan. Street-level board boundary: UNVERIFIED — FVREB publishes no public street-level boundary, and no municipal boundary was substituted for it. (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report)

Ground the live page works to, per the research: Whatcom Road (Highway 1 Exit 95), McKee Road, Old Clayburn Road, Laburnum Avenue, Marshall Road East and McMillan Road — modern hillside homes on Eagle Mountain and McKee Peak, executive view properties, family townhomes along Whatcom Road and Old Clayburn Road, and mature detached homes in McMillan. Highway 1 runs along the south side with access at Whatcom Road; main local roads also include Bateman Road and Sumas Way. There is no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station in Abbotsford.

Market context, labelled community context ONLY (SnapStats FVR Sep 2026; land has NO SnapStats category and no figure below is a land figure): Abbotsford East sub-area — Detached: inventory 165 (the highest detached inventory in Abbotsford), solds 15, ratio 9% (joint with Abbotsford West); "Condos & Townhomes" combined: 69 / 4 / 6% (the lowest published attached ratio in Abbotsford). Sub-area medians are not published (UNVERIFIED at sub-area level). Abbotsford community — Detached: 440 / 45 / median $949,000; combined attached: 572 / 58 / median $497,500.

Settled locator chains (SD34 settled all 13 addresses across the program's nine Abbotsford files; the two chains recorded for THIS sub-area, single-address only, non-transferable): 36367 Stephen Leacock Drive → Auguston Traditional Elementary / Clayburn Middle / Robert Bateman Secondary; 3836 Old Clayburn Road → Sandy Hill Elementary / Clayburn Middle / Robert Bateman Secondary (SD34 School Locator, run 2026-11-01). Every other Abbotsford East address's catchment is UNVERIFIED.

Transit: BC Transit routes 2 (Highstreet / McMillan), 7 (Sumas Mountain), 9 (McKee), 15 (Auguston), 16 (McMillan) and 26 (Sandy Hill / Bourquin school special), plus the 66 Fraser Valley Express on Highway 1.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Abbotsford East

items.t: OCP: Abbotsforward 2050 is CURRENT (adopted Dec 2025): 2600-2016, as updated" and live pages have carried "2500-2016" — both are stale/conflicted against the adopted 2050 plan; apply 2050 and flag both numbers as Jerry sweep items wherever a page carries them. The McKee Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 3400-2023) sits under it as Schedule E for the mountainside, and Clayburn Village is protected through a Heritage Conservation Area in the OCP.

Zoning: Abbotsford Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 governs: Lot-relevant zones as the research states them: RS3 (minimum interior lot 540 m²), RS5 (420 m²) and RS6 compact-lot. The zone section for the specific lot — not the neighbourhood name — decides whether a subdivision, a suite or added units are possible at all.

SSMUH / added units — NUMBER HELD UNCONFIRMED, conflict stated with both bases: 3560-2024, adopted June 25, 2024" (citing the program's rules-gaps pass and council minutes). Substance, as the research and City material state it: Zoning Bylaw s.140 carries the small-scale rules and s.140.3.8 permits one secondary suite in all single detached dwellings, with City-report criteria including a lot of at least 400 m², at least 12.0 m frontage, a Collector or Local road and not on a cul-de-sac bulb.

Secondary suites / coach and garden suites (Abbotsford's rules ONLY — never imported into other municipalities' files): a secondary suite must be less than 50% of the size of the principal unit to which it is accessory (changed from 100 m²), and garden suites and coach houses are allowed to occupy up to 15% of the lot area to a maximum of 100 m², under Zoning Bylaw 2014 No. 2400. No Bylaw 3100 exists. ( item 7f Abbotsford section)
Subdivision and servicing — process documented, NUMBER HELD UNCONFIRMED: Never quote a servicing standard for an east-side lot from a listing.

Slope / heritage diligence: the OCP includes a Steep Slope Development Permit Area for slope land — on McKee-area lots expect geotechnical conditions (the plan's open space network includes geotechnical areas and slopes over 40%) — and in Clayburn Village, confirm the Heritage Conservation Area rules before planning exterior changes.

Floodplain diligence: the low land at the south and southeast edge, toward Sumas Prairie, is floodplain land by the Sumas River; City flood notices name properties south of the Sumas River and along Whatcom Road in evacuation order and alert areas, and the OCP includes a Drainage and Flood Control map (Map 12). Check a low lot's status in the City's WebMap before offering.

ALR block (provincial frame, applied only where a parcel IS in the ALR): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tier — $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha / $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha / $10,000 under 0.8 ha, applications by Oct 31 — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR, and no farm-class claim is asserted for this sub-area.

faq.q: Which public schools are inside Abbotsford East?
faq.a: SD34 schools inside the area include Sandy Hill Elementary, Mountain Elementary, Irene Kelleher Totí:ltawtxw Elementary, Auguston Traditional Elementary, Clayburn Middle, Robert Bateman Secondary and Yale Secondary; use the SD34 School Locator with a home address to confirm the catchment school for that address. Locator runs for two sample addresses confirm the pattern: 36367 Stephen Leacock Drive returns Auguston Traditional Elementary → Clayburn Middle → Robert Bateman Secondary, and 3836 Old Clayburn Road returns Sandy Hill Elementary → Clayburn Middle → Robert Bateman Secondary (SD34 School Locator, mybaragar.com, run 2026-11-01).

faq.q: Which buses serve the east side?
faq.a: BC Transit Central Fraser Valley routes include 2 (Highstreet / McMillan), 7 (Sumas Mountain), 9 (McKee) and 15 (Auguston), plus the 66 Fraser Valley Express on Highway 1.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Abbotsford East than in June?
faq.a: In Abbotsford East, listings of houses rose from 161 in June to 165 in September (+2.5%); condos and townhomes fell from 71 in June to 69 in September (−2.8%).

faq.q: How big is Abbotsford East compared with the rest of Abbotsford?
faq.a: In September 2026, Abbotsford East held 37.5% of the 440 houses listed in Abbotsford and 12.1% of the 572 condos and townhomes listed in Abbotsford.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Abbotsford East from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 107 houses and 44 condos and townhomes sold in Abbotsford East over those 4 months.

faq.q: Can I buy a vacant building lot in Abbotsford East?
faq.a: What trades as land is fee-simple lots inside built subdivisions and individual acreage parcels toward Whatcom / Sumas Mountain, each checked parcel by parcel with the City.

faq.q: How small can an east-side lot be?
faq.a: At subdivision, the zone minimums the research states: RS3 interior 540 m², RS5 interior 420 m², RS6 compact (no minimum figure documented — UNCONFIRMED beyond "compact"). A lot already at its minimum has no subdivision room.

faq.q: Can a house lot here add a suite or a coach house?
faq.a: A secondary suite must be less than 50% of the principal unit, and a coach/garden suite may occupy up to 15% of the lot to a maximum of 100 m², under Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 — Abbotsford's rules only. Suite criteria in City reports include at least 400 m² lot, at least 12.0 m frontage, a Collector or Local road and not on a cul-de-sac bulb.

faq.q: What servicing will a subdivision have to provide?
faq.a: The process runs through the Approving Officer against zone minimums and the City's works-and-services requirements, with a servicing agreement and Works and Services Report as the standard instruments in council reports.

faq.q: What slope or flood diligence applies to a hillside or low lot?
faq.a: Hillside: the Steep Slope Development Permit Area and McKee geotechnical/slope-over-40% ground. Low south/southeast lots: Sumas River floodplain — City notices name properties south of the Sumas River and along Whatcom Road; check the lot in the City's WebMap.
